_source: CLAUDE.md §43 EXPERIMENT BUDGET and §44 OOS EXPOSURE. The seven counters, four bias accountings, four data states and five exposure triggers below are the spec's own lists, in its order and wording. scripts/tests/test_research_ledger.py parses them back out of CLAUDE.md.
_why_one_file: §43 and §44 are two sections over ONE structure: the experiment history. §43 counts what was tried; §44 asks what those tries did to the validation data. Splitting them into two registries would duplicate the period model in both, and the copy would drift the first time a period changed state -- which is exactly the failure §44 is about. One registry, two sections, per docs/../rules single-source-of-truth.
_reader: scripts/research_ledger.py is the ONE reader. Its inputs are the §42 experiment store (docs/experiments/) and this file's declared periods; it computes, it does not remember -- a counter kept by hand is a counter that disagrees with the store.

budget._spec: CLAUDE.md §43: 'Track experimentation scope. Do not hide the number of experiments performed.'

counters.definition: Distinct hypotheses filed, counted by their text. Two experiments testing the same hypothesis on different data are one hypothesis and two candidates.
Distinct candidate versions evaluated (§47's v1.x). This is the multiple-testing denominator.

Experiments whose `parameters` diff names a value that was SWEPT rather than chosen -- a range, a list, or several experiments differing only in one number. The distinction matters because a sweep of twenty values is twenty tests wearing one hypothesis.
How many times each dataset snapshot id has been read by an experiment. Reuse is not wrong; hiding it is, because every reuse lowers what an additional pass over the same data can tell you.
The same count restricted to periods declared out-of-sample. This is the number §44 turns into a state change.
Periods that have moved from `oos_untouched` to `oos_exposed`. Computed from the history, never asserted.
Candidates a human decided against. Recorded because a rejected candidate still consumed a test: §43's point is that the denominator includes everything that was tried, not everything that survived.

account_for.means: the more candidates are tested against one dataset, the more likely the best of them looks good by chance; the count is what makes that assessable
re-picking a winner from the same pool repeatedly is itself a fit to that pool
choices made after looking at the data -- a threshold, a target model, a symbol set -- are fitted to it even when no optimiser ran
the candidates that reach an experiment are already a selection, and the ones that were never filed are invisible to every statistic computed here

oos._spec: CLAUDE.md §44: 'Do not continue treating exposed OOS data as untouched validation data.'

states.means: data the candidate was built on. Nothing measured here is validation.

states.spec_name: OOS data that is still untouched
states.means: declared out-of-sample and not yet used for any choice. The only state in which an OOS result means what it claims.

states.spec_name: OOS data that has become exposed through candidate selection
states.means: it influenced a choice. It may still be reported -- it must not be reported as untouched validation.
reserved, never read, spent once. Reading it for anything other than a final confirmation converts it to `oos_exposed` like any other period.

oos._one_way: The transition is ONE-WAY. `oos_untouched -> oos_exposed` is allowed; the reverse raises. There is no cooling-off period and no 'it was only a look': §44 says 'do not label it as pristine validation anymore', and a state machine that can go back is a label that can be restored by whoever needs it to be.

oos._no_untouched_period_exists: There is currently NO period in `oos_untouched` or `final_holdout`. That is the honest state and it is stated rather than implied by an empty list: every span of history this repo holds has already been read by the runs that produced the live selection. A genuine OOS period has to be CARVED OUT and left alone before it can validate anything, and doing that is a decision about what the pilot trades, not a documentation change (§59).

fund_search.family_rule: the multiple-testing family is the CANDIDATE PROCEDURES (cells x methods = 6): grid values are not hypotheses (the nested walk-forward handles value selection); per-candidate primary bound = MIN of five one-sided bounds (iid t, CR1 by UTC date / 30-day window / calendar quarter / half-year), i.e. candidate p = MAX of the five one-sided p-values; floor confidence 1 - FAMILY_ALPHA/6 for every candidate; Holm step-down at FWER FAMILY_ALPHA over the six candidates at report time (a candidate with the k-th smallest p is rejected iff p_(k) <= FAMILY_ALPHA/(6-k+1) and every smaller p was rejected; NOT RUN and insufficient candidates enter with p = 1); the verdict rests on the floor test, so a candidate that fails the floor is never a PASS

evaluation_config.verdict_precedence: insufficient (any test fold < MIN_FOLD_TRADES, or fewer than MIN_TEST_FOLDS folds) overrides everything; otherwise pass only if EVERY check is ok (primary bound > 0 at the floor confidence 1 - 0.10/6, stability, frequency, D1-ADX regime split, ordinal perturbation, prop pass (unshifted, every fund), stress gate, minimum trading days), else fail; the prop pass with R shifted down by mean - bound is REPORT-ONLY and gates nothing. Holm's step-down over the six candidates is applied at report time and never turns a failing candidate into a pass
evaluation_config.regime_split: D1 ADX(14) (Wilder) of the last D1 bar whose CLOSE is at or before the entry time (close = max(open label + 24 h, next D1 open label); the entry day's forming bar is never read), from the symbol's own stored D1 series, point-in-time; split at the MEDIAN of the pooled TEST trades' values (<= median = low half, > median = high half); EACH half must hold at least 25 % of the pooled test trades (ties on one symbol-day ADX can leave a tiny half: 'regime halves unbalanced' fails the check); BOTH halves must have positive mean net R; a trade with no value fails the check

family.rule: the multiple-testing family is the CANDIDATE PROCEDURES (cells x methods = 6): grid values are not hypotheses (the nested walk-forward handles value selection); per-candidate primary bound = MIN of five one-sided bounds (iid t, CR1 by UTC date / 30-day window / calendar quarter / half-year), i.e. candidate p = MAX of the five one-sided p-values; floor confidence 1 - FAMILY_ALPHA/6 for every candidate; Holm step-down at FWER FAMILY_ALPHA over the six candidates at report time (a candidate with the k-th smallest p is rejected iff p_(k) <= FAMILY_ALPHA/(6-k+1) and every smaller p was rejected; NOT RUN and insufficient candidates enter with p = 1); the verdict rests on the floor test, so a candidate that fails the floor is never a PASS

perturbation.definition: ORDINAL components only (PERTURBATION_AXES), ONE component at a time, the other components at the fold's chosen values; each (component, direction) neighbour pools the test trades of the moved value sets (an edge has no neighbour on that side; a fold whose chosen value is not on the component's order, e.g. the v1-typed W4a baseline, is not perturbed and is reported); a neighbour passes iff its pooled mean net R > 0 AND its primary bound > 0 at the floor confidence; every neighbour must pass; categorical items are flipped and REPORTED, never gated

stress.definition: pooled mean net R must stay > 0 on the SAME admitted trades re-priced with the p90 spread (price-scaled, relative-spread profile) on both legs and a commission stress margin of 0.003 % of notional per round turn charged as 0.00003 * entry / |entry - stop| in R (a stress margin, NOT an estimate of FTMO's commission); admission is NOT re-run under stress; the stressed bound is reported, the gate is on the mean only

evaluation_config.prop_shift: REPORT-ONLY (owner decision 2026-10-02; not a gate, not in the verdict): prop_pass_probability recomputed for every fund with every pooled test trade's net R shifted DOWN by (pooled mean - primary bound at the floor confidence); the admitted trade list, sizing and horizon are unchanged; the UNSHIFTED prop pass >= 0.70 for every fund remains a gate

min_trading_days.definition: for EVERY fund of the prop gate whose account profile declares `min_trading_days` (FTMO Challenge Phase 1: 4, read from docs/architecture/account-profiles.json at evaluation time; the profile records the figure as flagged for verification: 2024+ sources report 4, older sources 10), EVERY test fold must contain at least that many DISTINCT UTC calendar days on which a pooled test trade was INITIATED (entry day, the reading account_profile.objectives uses); a fund without the field (The5ers High Stakes Step 1: min_profitable_days instead) is not checked; an unreadable or malformed profile fails the check (fail closed). A fold is 365 days while the challenge horizon is 120 resampled active days, so this is a NECESSARY-condition proxy for the objective, not a replay of the challenge. Owner decision 2026-10-02: a tightening, harmless in practice because every fold needs >= MIN_FOLD_TRADES trades

profile_note_flagged_for_verification.ftmo-challenge-phase1: 2024+ sources report 4 minimum trading days for FTMO Challenge Phase 1; older sources report 10. 4 recorded, flagged for verification per _source (docs/plans/2026-09-18-close-feature-gaps.md §0.1).

evaluation_config.ruin_handling: bt.RUIN_FRAC = 0.0 on the harness's own bt instance; post_ruin trades fail loud

embargo.rule: training trades need exit_label < test_start - 2 x H bars (H = bt.P[tf]['H']), on top of the one-bar purge; 'none' time stops are covered only by this same window

vc_volatility_condition.definition: decisive rows POINT IN TIME (lead decision D2 2026-10-04; sealed text §1-§2): edge_census.Series(sigma_every_day=True) events and VR, a signal on a server day's last bar dropped (as the paper log), stop k x sigma x sqrt(bars to the rollover on the clock) x price, book_sim's exit walk via fvg_forward.resolve_row; the research-mode book_sim rows are report-only
hypotheses: VC-a: the per-bar R of the H7 / G9 trend trades is higher on HIGH-volatility days (sigma_5m above the median of the previous 250 dense days that have one; F3 H5's rule, point in time)
VC-b: the per-bar R is higher for entries before the component's median entry slot (more bars left in the server day)

T1.gate: Holm, AND True-half mean R_net > 0, AND the balanced difference > 0 in both gold components; T1a ALSO needs the same contrast with the VR runs as clusters (T1a_run_clustered: CR1 by run, Student-t with min(runs per side x half cell) - 1 df) at one-sided p <= 0.05, and fails when that test cannot be computed (option C, lead decision 2026-10-05)
T1.statistic: side-balanced difference of nb-weighted R_bar cell means; T1a switched from R_gross at the seal (window B HIGH-LOW planned-bar gap 0.12 on the clock count, 0.149 on the stored count; rule: > 0.10)
